answer: Correlation-weighted aggregation fingerprints every submission's voyage (input-to-output trace), quill (authoring-tool metadata), and sparrow (canary-task response), then decays each identity's weight multiplicatively when its vectors match another identity too closely. An attacker pays a per-identity bond and price per attempt, faces a rate cap, and must wait epochs to earn trust, yet a coordinated ring shares pipeline artifacts, so similarity breaches threshold and aggregate weight collapses before quorum.
